cohort: 36 women with histologically proven abnormally invasive placenta: 6 treated with total hysterectomy and 30 treated with supracervical hysterectomy
finding: In cases of abnormally invasive placenta managed operatively, supracervical hysterectomy was associated with lower blood product utilization compared to total hysterectomy without significant differences in operative time, hospitalization time, or maternal and neonatal outcomes.
